summary: Track passes this round: score 8/10, no blocker or major issue. I re-checked all 12 r1-tech issues in the browser, and all 12 now behave correctly. Two parts are still open: the major missed its 'no task over ~100 ms' target (one ~250 ms task remains, issue 2), and the NaN case and vertex scan the fixes asked for were never added to the unit's own tests (issue 6). Major (load stall): fixed. The O(r²) search is gone: the kd-tree (layout/sample-index.ts) now accounts for 30-80 ms of samples per profiled restart, instead of 1738 ms of self time in r1. The build yields between stages and emits flow:loading. The worst rAF gap during a restart dropped from 2000 ms to 224 ms with all units (351 ms with stubs), measured under load avg 20-30. One ~250 ms makeHull task remains (issue 2). Minors, re-verified: (1) Tunnel lighting: unlit baked shell, same look at low and high, no acne. (2) Invisible wall at the cutting: edges.mjs gives wallMissing 0, wallInside 0, wallOk 3188, and the road surface 0 mm / 0 misses over 12,243 raycasts. (3) Quay posts and sign overhang: waterBlocked 0; below 2.6 m the only intrusion is the known ≤ 7 cm banked-rail lean. (4) Failed builds: an injected fillText failure logs '[track] build failed', tears down and rethrows, and core falls back to the stub world. (5) Crowd/boats: no longer cast shadows. (6) quality=low: env drops from 166 calls / 739k tris to 93 / 423k. (7) Duplicated search and fog cull: now shared. (8) Dead code: removed. (9) Logs: only with ?debug. (10) project(NaN): returns {s: 0, x: 0, y: 0} and warns once. (11) flow:loading: progress 0.12→0.9. Engineering status: tsc reports 0 errors, there is no 'any', the largest file is 243 lines, and the console shows 0 errors in every run (Chromium and WebKit). Contract: frameAt/bounds/surfaceAt clamp NaN, ±∞ and out-of-range s; runoff is 250 m; the self-test round trip is within 2.6 mm. project() returns the true nearest point even with hints off by 10-1000 m over 3000 points; it costs 1.2-1.6 µs per call. Sign conventions match core/types.ts: curvature, bank and right = tangent × up, with 0 of 420 curvature mismatches. The only sharp vertical curvature is the designed jumpCrest (3.8°/m at s 1640, launches above 12.2 m/s). Leaks: none over 4 consecutive races, then quit → menu. With all units geometries settle at about 370-380, textures 44, programs 58 and heap 39 MB. With stubs, quitting returns to geometries 0, textures 1, programs 2. Determinism: geometry, feature and query hashes are identical for seeds 1/2/1 and in a fresh page. Performance at 1920×1080: a steady 120 fps (p95 10.2 ms), track.update 0.05 ms per frame, environment ≤ 166 calls / 739k tris including the shadow pass. There are no fog-cull pops: 4 toggles changed pixels along the whole track, and the largest changed 39 px. The track's own materials caused no mid-race shader compiles. Remaining issues, all minor: font and billboard-art waits time out silently and are never redrawn, which makes the sign atlas depend on timing; one long dressing task; aliased shallow-sea bands from a coarse, stretched height map; sub-pixel hulls drawn to the fog limit, with medium the same as high; a renderHeightMap without try/finally; no regression scripts in the unit; a curb mismatch of up to 1.5 m at run ends; small hygiene items; and a cross-unit compile hitch. Evidence and scripts are in shots/review/track/r2-tech/.

issues.title: Font and billboard-art waits are timed and silent, and are never redrawn: under load the signs bake fallback content and the atlas depends on timing
issues.detail: fonts.ts:16-35 waits at most 2.5 s for the CJK glyph slices. It is awaited twice in a row: track.ts:70, then dressing/coast/index.ts:67. One build fetches about 130 woff2 slices (fontslow.mjs counted the requests). Over 4 cold loads on this machine (load avg about 30, fonts3.mjs), 3 printed '[track] fonts still loading after 2500 ms' (one of them twice) and the coast build took 6.5-9.8 s. When the wait times out, the canvases are drawn with fallback glyphs and stay that way: in fontslow.mjs the fonts were loaded 8 s later, but the atlas was never redrawn (atlas-compare.jpg: the 鹈鹕岬隧道 plate uses fallback glyphs). loadBillboardArt (dressing/coast/signage.ts:13-29) is worse: Promise.race against a timeout that resolves [] drops every image, including the ones that already loaded, and logs nothing. With the webp files delayed 3 s (artslow.mjs), all 6 posters lost their art (atlas-art-compare.jpg) and 0 warnings were printed. As a result the sign atlas depends on timing. determinism.mjs: same seed 1 in two fresh pages gave atlas hashes 879916168 vs 894359872, while the geometry/feature/query hashes were identical. atlas.mjs: 3 cold pages without timeouts gave byte-identical atlases.
issues.fix: Export the optional preload(app) from src/world/index.ts. Core already awaits unit preloads in main.ts:15. Use it to warm the union of all sign texts with document.fonts.load and to decode the billboard art once per app with img.decode(). Start a single ensureFonts at the top of createTrack so the download overlaps the CPU stages. In loadBillboardArt, put a timeout on each image (Promise.allSettled), keep every image that loaded, and console.warn when an image times out. If fonts or art arrive after the build (document.fonts 'loadingdone' or a late img.onload), redraw the affected faces and set faceTex.needsUpdate.

issues.title: r1 load stall mostly fixed, but one ~250 ms task remains in the dressing (makeHull with string keys), and progress sits at 0.62 for most of the build
issues.detail: Restart, all units, stall2.mjs (3 runs, load avg about 20). Long tasks of 131/126/115/92 ms happen at the ROAD/HILLS/SEA/PROPS stages. A 240-265 ms task follows inside the dressing (PROPS 0.62 at about 830 ms, READY 0.9 at 1480-1620 ms). The worst rAF gap is 224 ms with all units and 351 ms with stubs (loadstall-*.json); r1 measured 2000 ms. profile2.mjs shows a 444 ms busy run in which PropBatch.finish takes 344 ms and makeHull (world/geom.ts:130-158) 252 ms. makeHull builds two template-string keys per vertex for a Map<string, Vector3>, and the 'props' batch holds 733k vertices (xforms.mjs). finishDressYielding (dressing/dress.ts:77-85) yields only between batches, so the whole 'props' batch is one task. The loading bar shows 0.62 for 650-750 ms, while the stage that takes about 60 % of the build runs.
issues.fix: Weld vertices with numeric keys in makeHull: quantise to Int32 and hash into an Int32Array open-addressing table, or sort the indices once. That should be 5-10× faster. Also yield inside PropBatch.finish every ~8 cells (make finish async or a generator), and emit flow:loading 0.62→0.88 in steps from the coast dressing. Budget: no track task over 100 ms. Assert it in a script.

issues.title: Sea shallow bands and surf alias into staircases: the 1024² height map covers 1920×5376 m (1.9×5.3 m texels)
issues.detail: env/heightmap.ts renders the whole far-grid box into a square 1024×1024 half-float target. hm.mjs reads W 1920 m and D 5376 m, so texels are 1.88 × 5.25 m (2.8:1). env/sea.ts makes the colour bands with hard thresholds on depth (dd < 1.4 / 5.5 / 11). It derives toShore from a central difference over one texel of that coarse map. Bilinear height plus hard steps gives blocky staircase band contours and broken surf strips. They are visible from the cliff/crest cameras and from any elevated view (foam-sheet.jpg and foam-crop.jpg at s 230 and 2600, camera 14 m up). The ripple and sparkle terms are bare step() calls with no derivative anti-aliasing, so they shimmer at 50-400 m in motion.
issues.fix: Fit the height map to the water's edge: render only a ~300 m band around the shore/water edges, or use a target that matches the aspect (1024×2048 or 2048×4096 at high). Anti-alias every threshold: float aa = fwidth(dd); col bands via smoothstep(t - aa, t + aa, dd). Do the same for the step() calls on rip, sparkle, rolling and shore.

issues.title: Perf headroom: sub-pixel outline hulls are drawn to the fog limit, medium = high, and the sign atlas is not scaled
issues.detail: perf.mjs (1920×1080, high, incl. shadow pass): environment peak 166 calls / 739k tris at s 2416. That is 92 % of the brief's 800k (r1 peak was 581k); the whole game peaks at 229 calls / 1.0 M. hulls.mjs at s 2416: 159k hull triangles sit in cells whose nearest point is more than 120 m away, where the 0.04 m outline is under 0.35 px wide. Only 46k hull triangles are nearer. Medium is the same scene as high: 164 calls / 695k vs 166 / 739k; only the shadow map changes. Low is 93 / 423k. The 2048×3072 sign atlas (about 33 MB with mipmaps, 2324 of 3072 rows used) is the same at every quality. FPS is fine today: a steady 120 fps with p95 10.2 ms, and track.update 0.05 ms per frame (fps.mjs).
issues.fix: In world/lod.ts also hide each mesh's userData.isOutline child when its bounding sphere is more than ~130 m from the camera; this saves about 150k tris per frame for free. At medium, drop hulls on far/cover/thin cards and skip half the ground cover. Size the atlas to its used height (2048×2560), or 1024 wide at low.

issues.title: renderHeightMap is not exception-safe: it re-parents the group and rebinds the shared renderer without try/finally
issues.detail: env/heightmap.ts:38-66 does these steps in sequence: hide every non-heightmap mesh, move the track group into a temporary scene, setRenderTarget(half-float target), setClearColor(black), render. If renderer.render throws (context loss, shader compile failure), the shared WebGLRenderer stays bound to the track's render target with a black clear colour, and the meshes stay hidden. createTrack's teardown (track.ts:41-48) disposes the target but does not restore renderer state. Everything rendered afterwards, including the core stub fallback, goes into the stale off-screen target instead of the canvas.
issues.fix: Put the render in try { … } finally { restore render target, clear colour/alpha, visibility, parent }. Optionally validate the target with renderer.getContext().checkFramebufferStatus and fall back to a flat 'deep' height map with a console.warn.

issues.title: The r1 fixes have no regression coverage in the unit; the verification numbers come from the critic's gitignored scratch scripts
issues.detail: status/track.md 'Verified (fix round 1)' cites edges.mjs, intrude2.mjs and loadstall.mjs. These are the r1 critic's scratch scripts in shots/review/track/r1-tech/, which is gitignored and not owned by the unit. The r1 fixes explicitly asked for the vertex scan and the project(NaN) case in sandbox/track.test.mjs. Neither was added: the test still checks only frame NaNs, round trips, bounds/surface sanity and the dispose leak. Nothing in the unit's own tooling guards the invisible-wall, sign-overhang, NaN or load-stall fixes against regressions.
issues.fix: Add sandbox/track.audit.mjs (or extend track.test.mjs) with exit codes for: sideways raycasts at bounds() (wallMissing = 0, waterBlocked = 0), the vertex-intrusion scan (≤ 0.08 m below 2.6 m), project({x: NaN}) → finite {s: clamp(hint), x: 0, y: 0}, and a restart long-task budget (≤ 150 ms). Document it under 'How to test'.

issues.title: surfaceAt reports 'curb' up to 1.5 m past the end of the drawn curb blocks
issues.detail: curbs-water.mjs raycast 4400 curb samples. 14 mismatch, all at run ends: s 682.0, 710.5, 986.5, 1712.5, 2327.5, 2570.5 … on both sides surfaceAt returns 'curb' (rumble in physics) but no curb mesh is drawn there. surfaceAt reads the per-1 m flag at Math.round(s - sMin) (query.ts:189-190). road.ts buildCurbs draws 1.5 m blocks only where both block ends are flagged (road.ts:89-91), so each drawn strip stops up to 1.5 m before its flagged run ends. Tiny in metres, but it is a bounds/visual mismatch, which the brief forbids.
issues.fix: Make both sides use one rule: either snap the curb flags to whole 1.5 m blocks in TrackQuery.markCurbs, so surfaceAt sees exactly the drawn blocks, or let buildCurbs emit a partial last block up to the final flagged sample. Add the curb raycast to the audit script.

issues.title: Code hygiene: type escapes, a cast-typed string array, a hot-path allocation, long lines
issues.detail: layout/query.ts:85 builds the TrackFrame with 'as unknown as TrackFrame'. terrain/far.ts:72 stores materials in new Array<string> and casts them back at line 135. TrackQuery.surfaceAt allocates a {sd, curb} object per call through side() (query.ts:152,188); physics calls it per rider per 120 Hz substep, and bounds() also allocates. Lines run to 188 chars (features/bridge.ts:11), 179 (scenery/signs/boards.ts:56) and 166 (terrain/near.ts:132), although r1 asked for about 140. roadRange, SHOULDER_COLORS and tunnelOutline are exported but only used inside their own files.
issues.fix: Construct the frame with real fields: {s: 0, pos: new Vector3(), …, halfWidth: 0}. Type M as a MatKind[] (or a Uint8Array of enum indices). Return the side arrays through two private fields or inline the ternary in surfaceAt. Wrap lines at ~140 and drop the unused exports.

issues.title: cross-unit: no shader precompile at race start; a 383 ms hitch hits mid-race when rival bike/rider programs compile on first sight
issues.detail: hitch.mjs ran a full real-time autopilot race at 1920×1080 (sim ×2, 10,134 frames, p50 8 ms, p99 10 ms) with exactly one frame over 50 ms: 383 ms at s ≈ 418. That is the frame right after renderer.info.programs gained bikes:depth ×2, bikes:body and actors:rider. No track material compiled during the race. Nothing calls renderer.compile/compileAsync (grep).
issues.fix: Core request: in game.ts, before show('race'), await app.renderer.compileAsync(app.scene, app.camera) with every session object temporarily visible, or have the bikes/actors preload warm their materials.
